summary: Rustler Peak in Jackson County: lookout site since 1913; present L-4 cab on a 1948 laminated timber tower; staffed in fire season as of 2021; standing in 2021.

facts.design: L-4 14 by 14 foot cab on a laminated timber tower

access.note: Cheryl Hill's standing list marks it accessible to the public. Forest roads reach a gate; the last mile is a gated road walk. Staffed by a lookout attendant in fire season.

visit.trail_note: Park in a pullout before the gate and walk the last mile. Climb the tower only if the attendant invites you.

events.note: Register says the site was a full lookout by 1913, first lookout named in the Register entry
Pre-cut D-6 lookout house assembled in July 1917; a 1917 Ashland report said it would sit on an 18-foot steel tower
D-6 cupola cabin on a 10-foot steel tower; firelookout.com dates it 1920, the Register says 1920s
Mrs. Blossom Smith went to live at the station for the summer
CCC spent $600 on lookout construction; the cupola was raised onto a tower
Lookout posted because of lightning danger, May 29
Mr. and Mrs. Howard Greer manning the lookout; had manned it for three years by September 1960
Present L-4 cab on a laminated timber tower, 31 feet 6 inches per Register and Forest Lookouts (firelookout.com says 30 feet)
Site of the first solar-powered radio system in a Forest Service lookout
Contractors installed a modern vault toilet at the site

corrections.why: The Register gives the present 1948 tower as 31'6" (about 9.6 m). The record's 3.0 m matches the 10-foot tower of the 1920s, which was earlier than the present one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1948 is the present L-4 cab. The site had lookouts from 1913, a 1917 D-6 house and a 1920s cupola. Sources disagree on the height of the 1917 and 1920s tower: 18 feet in a 1917 newspaper item and the 2021 trip report, 10 feet in the Register and firelookout.com.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 3.0 looks wrong: the 1948 tower is 31'6" per the Register and Forest Lookouts (9.6 m); firelookout.com says 30 feet (9.1 m). Proposed 9.6 m is a correction for review, and facts.height_m uses it. Elevation: Register 6,154 ft (1,876 m) against 6,208 ft on firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill's list; the record's 1,875.7 m matches the Register and is kept. Name and spelling: the Register names William Parker as first lookout; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1915 item naming a Ray Parker; the Register's 1917 contractor (Mill-Made) and the newspaper quote (Mill-Maid) differ. Forest: the Register and firelookout.com say Rogue River National Forest; Cheryl Hill and the trip report say Rogue River-Siskiyou. The 2021 trip report is dated August 14, 2021 on the tag page; a March 2, 2025 date also appears beside it and was not checked further. Current staffing and access rest on a 2021 trip report and undated lists; no 2025 or 2026 source found, so recheck with the Butte Falls Ranger District. No photos added.
